ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an AC power supply supplying power through a transformer, marked about 220 V, 50 Hz; the transformer secondary side is labeled U2. After the secondary side is connected a bridge rectifier circuit composed of four diodes. A capacitor C is connected in parallel at the rectified output end, and the load resistor RL is also connected to the same output end; on the right side, the positive and negative poles of the output voltage U0 are marked. Therefore this circuit is a single-phase bridge rectifier parallel capacitor filter circuit, not a pure bridge rectifier circuit. Reasoning: The problem gives U2 = 12 V, RL = 100 Ω, but does not give the capacitance value, so calculate according to the commonly used approximate formula for this type of bridge rectifier capacitor filter circuit: U0 ≈ 1.2U2. Substituting U2 = 12 V gives U0 ≈ 1.2 × 12 = 14.4 V.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify that this is not a plain bridge rectifier but a bridge rectifier with a shunt capacitor filter across the load. From the text, take U_2 = 12 V; R_L is given but no capacitance is supplied, so use the standard approximate design formula for this circuit. Compute U_0 ≈ 1.2 × 12 = 14.4 V.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that the capacitor filter charges to near the peak of the rectified secondary voltage and supplies the 100 Ω load between peaks. From the text, use U_2 = 12 V RMS. Estimate the peak as U_m = sqrt(2)×12 ≈ 17.0 V, then apply the ordinary loaded capacitor-filter allowance, U_0 ≈ 0.85U_m ≈ 0.85×17.0 ≈ 14.4 V.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是单相桥式整流电容滤波电路。左侧为交流输入约220V、50Hz，经变压器后在次级标出电压 U2；中间是桥式整流器；右侧输出端并联有滤波电容 C 和负载电阻 RL，负载两端标出输出电压 U0，极性上正下负。推理：题给 U2 = 12V，按交流有效值处理。电容滤波时，电容会充到接近整流后二次侧电压峰值，并在峰值间向 RL=100Ω 负载供电。二次侧峰值 Um = sqrt(2) × 12 ≈ 16.97V。按普通有载电容滤波估算，输出直流电压 U0 ≈ 0.85Um ≈ 0.85 × 16.97 ≈ 14.4V。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Weakly distinct physical-estimate route: instead of starting from the 1.2 coefficient as a memorized formula, it interprets the capacitor as charging near the AC peak and then uses the usual ripple/loss allowance for a loaded capacitor-input bridge to arrive at the same effective factor.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram to confirm a full-wave bridge, meaning two diodes conduct per charging interval, and a capacitor is directly across the DC output/load, so the capacitor holds the output near the secondary peak rather than the unfiltered average.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use U_2 = 12 V as the transformer secondary RMS voltage and R_L = 100 Ω only to confirm the circuit is under load; no capacitance is provided, so an approximate empirical allowance is required.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A 12 V transformer secondary is an RMS value; its peak is sqrt(2)U_2. In a practical loaded bridge with capacitor filtering, diode conduction drops and discharge ripple make the average DC output somewhat below the peak, conventionally approximated as about 0.85 of the peak, equivalent to about 1.2U_2.
